desc: How hard a hit flinches a Hunter (Oomph.hit_strength, Oomph.flinch_weight). Strength hit_k = chip_k + damage share of max health * frac_k + knock (m/s) * knock_k, from chip_k up to Oomph.HEAVY_FLINCH; a big hit (stagger) is always the heaviest. The body's spring (HunterAnim) scales by hit_k; the clip hero's base additive flinch layer (WardenClips) plays `light` of the hit clip on a chip hit and all of it by a stagger, which takes the whole body. Source-quality weight: a chip hit never looks like a knockdown, a big one is never a twitch.

hit_slow.doc: The slow when you are hit by a rival (Oomph.react, reference tuning; hits from monsters never slow, so PvE lethality is unchanged). big: one hit of at least big_frac of max health (or a heavy, payoff or stun hit) staggers: speed x big_mult for big_s, x big_repeat_mult if the last big hit was within repeat_s. small: hit damage adds up and resets after sum_reset_s without a hit; once it reaches small_frac of max health you are slowed x small_mult for small_s (x small_mult_armor for small_s_armor while you have armour left), then no new small slow for small_cd_s. The strongest slow still wins (Ent). floor_ms: a hit slow never takes the base walk under this (m/s, the reference value x body_scale); a Hunter already slower is not slowed. last_alive_small/big: added to the multiplier for the last one up on a squad (LastAlive), at most last_alive_cap. small_frac keeps the reference's small/big ratio (150/400) on our big_frac.
